chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from 'Asim, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'An angel came to me and said, "O Muhammad, your Lord sends you greetings and says to you: If you wish, I will turn the plains of Makkah into nuggets of gold."' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) raised his head to the sky and said, 'O Lord, I am sated one day so I praise You, and I am hungry another day so I implore You.'

key_terms.بِطْحَاءَ مَكَّةَ: The plains or open areas of Makkah

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say when offered the gold of Mecca?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) is offered the immense wealth of the world, specifically gold covering the plains of Mecca, as a divine test. He accepts this provision not as a rejection of wealth, but as a strategic choice for spiritual balance: satiety allows for gratitude (*shukr*), while hunger fosters supplication (*du'a*). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) as a means to maintain spiritual vigilance rather than mere poverty.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 19.Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar (a) who said, “

The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) said, ‘An angel came and told me, “O Muḥammad, your Lord sends you greetings and says to you: If you wish, I will turn the plains of Makkah into nuggets of gold [for you].”’ So the Prophet (ṣ) raised his head to the sky and said, ‘O Lord, I am sated one day so I praise You, and I am hungry another day so I implore You [and that is enough for me].’”
